answer_to_review: Codex asked that the next acceptable stage be tied to a real Studio consumer instead of more helper depth. This is that consumer.

result.what_it_is: game/studio/StudioAuthoringAuditSection.cs, a Studio section that writes nothing and explains: for the current selection it lists AuthoringDiagnostics' steps (what the runtime will do and which link is missing), and for the workspace it lists the kind-to-consumer map plus the kinds nothing claims by name
result.shared_file: the section is registered by ONE line in StudioRoot.cs, which is Codex's shared file, so that line is handed as a patch and NOT applied by me: authoring-audit-section.patch contains the new file and the one-line hook
result.closure_for_cherry_pick: the consumer needs seven of my Core projection files that main does not have yet: TriggerScopeFacts, AuthoringDiagnostics, ItemSpawns, AssetUsageIndex, CutsceneActions, SimpleItemForms and PcChatContent. That closure was measured, not guessed: pristine main plus exactly those files builds Urman.Studio.Core with 0 errors, and the missing pieces were found by compiling and reading the errors
result.honesty: without those seven files the section cannot be integrated, and the panel is a consumer, not a finished editor: it reads and explains, and every write still goes through the shared EditSession
